intro: Birthdays, weddings and important dates of the year in Spain.
p.fiesta.consejo: «Estar de fiesta» means having fun. It is also an official day off: «un día de fiesta».
p.boda.consejo: You say «ir a una boda». The «novios» are the two people getting married.
p.Navidad.consejo: It takes a capital and is singular: «la Navidad». «Las Navidades» are the whole holiday period.
p.Nochebuena.consejo: It is written as one word. Many families have a long dinner that night.
p.Nochevieja.consejo: It is the «old night», the last of the year. It is written as one word and v sounds like b.
p.Reyes Magos.consejo: It is shortened to «los Reyes»: «el día de Reyes». It is always plural.
p.regalar.consejo: The person who gets the gift goes with «le»: «le regalo flores a mi madre».
p.invitar.consejo: You say «invitar a alguien a algo»: «te invito a mi fiesta». It also means paying: «te invito a un café».
p.celebrar.consejo: You celebrate a birthday or a wedding. The verb is regular: «celebro», «celebras».
p.brindar.consejo: You say «brindar por algo»: «brindamos por tu cumpleaños». When toasting you say «¡salud!».
p.tarta.consejo: In Spain it is «tarta»; in many Latin American countries it is «pastel» or «torta».
p.velas.consejo: On a birthday cake you «blow» the candles. A «vela» is also a boat's sail.
p.uvas.consejo: On New Year's Eve people eat twelve «uvas», one with each chime. The u sounds as in «uno».
p.felicidades.consejo: It is always plural: «¡felicidades!». It is said on birthdays, at weddings and with good news.
b1.texto:
- **Nochebuena**, 24 December: many families have a long dinner.
- **Navidad**, 25 December.
- **Nochevieja**, 31 December: people eat twelve **uvas**, one with each chime at midnight.
- **Reyes Magos**, 6 January: on that day children receive presents.

For a birthday you say **¡Feliz cumpleaños!** or **¡Felicidades!** There is a **tarta** with **velas**.

The verbs: **celebrar** a birthday; **invitar** someone to a party; **regalar** something to someone; **brindar** to something: ¡salud!
b2.f0.texto: This Saturday I am celebrating my birthday.
b2.f1.texto: I invite you to the party.
b2.f6.texto: At twelve we are going to make a toast.
b4.texto:
These verbs take a fixed small word:

- **invitar a** someone **a** something: **te invito a mi fiesta**.
- **regalar** something **a** someone: the person who receives the gift is said with **le** or **les**: **le regalo una tarta a Lucía**.
- **brindar por** something: **brindamos por tu cumpleaños**.
- **celebrar** something, with no small word: **celebro mi cumpleaños**.

For a near plan we use **ir a + infinitive**: **vamos a brindar**.
b4.e0.texto: I invite my friends to the party.
b4.e2.texto: We make a toast to your birthday.
b5.titulo: The night of the twelve grapes
b5.f0.texto: The family table shines under the lights of the living room.
b5.f1.texto: The grandparents place twelve round grapes on each plate.
b5.f2.texto: The children watch the clock with their eyes wide open.
b5.f3.texto: The chimes ring one by one in the silence of the night.
b5.f4.texto: Each sweet grape fills the mouth with a fresh taste.
b5.f5.texto: At twelve everyone hugs in the middle of the living room.
b5.f6.texto: The glasses clink with a clear, bright sound.
b5.f7.texto: The neighbours wave from the open windows with cheerful voices.
b5.f8.texto: Outside, the fireworks paint the sky red and gold.
b5.f9.texto: A tired girl smiles in her father's arms.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! It is the «old night»: the last of the year.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is the night of 24 December.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Invitar en» is not said. This verb takes «a».
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done! You say «invitar a alguien a una fiesta».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Para» shows purpose. With invitar you use «a».
b7.pregunta: Which word is missing to invite someone?
b8.traduccion: This Saturday I am celebrating my birthday
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is for a birthday, not for New Year's Eve.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Candles are not eaten. On New Year's Eve people eat fruit.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! One grape with each chime.
b9.pregunta: What do people eat at twelve on New Year's Eve?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Correct! «Le» stands for Lucía, even though she is a woman.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «La» is for direct objects. The person who gets the gift takes «le».
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Se» only appears before «lo» or «la»: «se lo regalo».
b10.pregunta: Which word goes with the person who gets the gift?
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Regalar» is giving something to someone, not raising a glass.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That's it! You toast with «¡salud!» and your glasses up.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Invitar» is asking someone to come or paying for them.
b12.pregunta: Which verb do you use when raising the glass?
p.celebro.consejo: Verb «celebrar». The c before «e» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.invito.consejo: In Spanish «v» sounds like «b», so it is «im-BI-to». The infinitive is «invitar».
p.brindamos.consejo: «Brindar» means to raise a glass. The «d» between vowels is soft.
p.colocan.consejo: The «c» before «o» is hard, like «k». The stress falls on «LO».
p.abiertos.consejo: «ie» forms a diphthong in an unstressed syllable, so it is «BYER». It comes from «abrir».
p.campanadas.consejo: It comes from «campana» (bell). On New Year's Eve Spain hears twelve chimes.
p.uva.consejo: The «v» sounds like «b», so it is «U-ba». On New Year's Eve you eat one per chime.
p.sabor.consejo: It ends in the consonant -r, so the stress is on the last syllable: «sa-BOR».
p.chocan.consejo: «Chocar» also means to clink glasses. The «ch» is a single sound, as in «church».
p.pintan.consejo: Here «pintar» means colouring the sky. Think of fireworks lighting up the night.
